questions.question: X pays loss one with probability 0.2 and zero otherwise; Y pays one with probability 0.4 and zero otherwise. What stochastic comparison holds?
options: $Y\le_{\mathrm{st}}X$ and the laws differ.
Both weak orders hold because their supports agree.
Neither weak order holds because both have atoms.
$X\le_{\mathrm{st}}Y$ and the laws differ.

questions.question: A loss X is certainly 2. Loss Y takes 2 or 5 with equal probability. Which comparison follows from their CDFs?
options: $Y\le_{\mathrm{st}}X$.
$X\le_{\mathrm{st}}Y$.
Both orders hold because both can pay 2.
Neither order holds because X is deterministic.

questions.question: On support 0,1,2, X has probabilities(0.5,0.3,0.2) and Y has(0.2,0.4,0.4). Which full stochastic comparison follows?
options: The larger Y CDF establishes only the Y-to-X stochastic direction.
The two complete CDFs agree at every threshold.
The larger X CDF establishes only the X-to-Y stochastic direction.
The cumulative comparisons reverse inside the support.

questions.question: Non-negative losses are transformed by the increasing cap $h(z)=\min(z,1)$. If h(X) and h(Y) have identical laws, can their original laws still be different?
options: No; increasing maps are always invertible on their domains.
No; equal transformed laws force equal original CDFs.
Yes; distinct losses above 1 can all map to 1.
Yes; but only when h is decreasing somewhere.

questions.question: X is 0 or 2 equally likely and Y is 1 or 3 equally likely. Add the same fee 4 to both. At threshold 5, what are the CDFs of X+4 and Y+4?
options: Both equal 1/2.
They are 1 and 1/2.
They are 1/2 and 0.
They are 0 and 1/2.

questions.question: X is uniform on[0,2] and Y uniform on[1,3]. Their CDFs are linear from 0 to 1 on those intervals and constant outside. Which conclusion follows from checking the overlap[1,2] and both nonoverlap regions?
options: Their overlapping supports prevent a stochastic comparison.
The one-unit shift makes Y the stochastically larger loss.
The one-unit shift makes X the stochastically larger loss.
Equal interval lengths make their full CDFs identical.
